title: US Suspends Cognizant's Green Card Filings Amid Federal Fraud Investigation
excerpt: The Labor Department has blocked the IT giant from filing new PERM applications as federal authorities investigate alleged fraud involving H-1B and employment-based immigration programmes.
body:
• The US Department of Labor has suspended Cognizant's PERM filings, blocking the company from sponsoring new employment-based green cards for foreign workers.
  • Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito announced the action alongside the White House Fraud Task Force, warning that "handcuffs await" those involved in fraud.
  • Cloudera's PERM filings have also been suspended as part of the broader immigration-fraud scrutiny.
  • The suspension affects new filings only and does not cancel existing green card applications or H-1B statuses already in place.

The US Department of Labor has suspended Cognizant Technology Solutions from filing new permanent labour certification applications, cutting off a critical step in the employment-based green card process for the India-founded IT services giant.

Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito announced the action on September 8 in a post on X, declaring that his office and the White House Fraud Task Force were jointly investigating the company.

"Cognizant's PERM filings are suspended. Threats to American workers will NOT be tolerated. Alongside @WHFraudTF, we're following facts, fraud and finances. Handcuffs await."

— Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito

What PERM Means for Workers

PERM, or Program Electronic Review Management, is the labour certification process that US employers must complete before sponsoring foreign workers for permanent residency. The employer must demonstrate that no qualified American workers are available for the position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect wages or working conditions.

The suspension means Cognizant cannot submit new PERM filings while the investigation continues. It does not, by itself, revoke previously approved green cards or affect existing H-1B statuses.

Investigation Spans Multiple Agencies

D'Esposito said his office was working with Labor Department officials and the White House anti-fraud task force, though he did not disclose the specific allegations against Cognizant, the number of applications affected or the expected duration of the suspension. One report cited a 180-day freeze, but the Labor Department has not publicly confirmed the timeline.

The investigation is examining allegations that include fraudulent visa applications, wage violations, exploitation of foreign workers and practices that could undermine American workers. However, authorities have not announced any criminal charges or a formal finding of wrongdoing.

Cloudera Also Hit

Cognizant is not the only company affected. D'Esposito separately announced that PERM filings by Cloudera had also been suspended. "One more. @cloudera: PERM filings SUSPENDED," he wrote.

Cognizant Touts US Hiring Push

The suspension came just a day after Cognizant announced plans to expand its American workforce, pledging to hire 1,500 US college graduates and grow its Frontier Certified Engineer and Frontier Business Operator workforce to 15,000 people.

"We are hiring American graduates, standing up new American job categories for the AI era, and putting Cognizant's capital and leadership behind a national coalition built to make sure this transition works for workers," CEO Ravi Kumar S said. The company also said it had joined RAISE US, a bipartisan coalition focused on helping American workers transition into the artificial intelligence economy.

What It Means for Indian Tech Workers

Cognizant, founded in Chennai in 1994 and now headquartered in Teaneck, New Jersey, remains one of the largest corporate users of the H-1B visa programme despite a significant decline in approvals — from 9,413 in 2020 to 3,510 as of June 2026.

For the thousands of Indian technology professionals whose long-term US residency plans depend on employer-sponsored PERM filings, the suspension creates immediate uncertainty. Workers already in the green card pipeline may face delays if Cognizant cannot initiate new certifications, and the broader scrutiny could ripple across the Indian IT services sector as other major firms — including TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCL Technologies — watch whether similar action follows.

The investigation remains ongoing. Until authorities release additional findings, the allegations against Cognizant remain unproven.
